== Research Notes ==
=== Currituck will review, 23 October 2026 ===

The named daughter Ruth matches the Currituck child and six siblings under the William/Sarah couple. Her later residence and lifespan remain separately sourced claims. Existing father William Glasgow-357: '''54% → 97% confident'''. These percentages assess each existing child-to-William profile pair from the combined named household, locality and compatible generation; they are subjective, not measured frequencies. The will proves the stated father roles through a checked transcription, not the children’s exact birthdays, later migrations, spouses or descendants. Sarah is named as William’s wife, not explicitly as every child’s mother, and her Cooper maiden surname is not supplied. All maternal assessments remain separate. William’s own Caleb-363 father hypothesis stays 29%. No father is newly attached and no profile is merged.

William Glasgow’s Currituck will, dated 14 October 1805 and recorded 22 January 1806, names wife Sarah, sons Caleb, Isaac, Samuel and John C., and daughters Ruth, Love Bright and Sophia. Its land divisions and household bequests identify one specific family. The named wife and all seven child names strongly identify the maintained William-357 family, with John C. compatible with John Cooper and Love now recorded under Bright; this conjunction outweighs the unsourced August death claim. The published transcription is by Judy Merrell Brickhouse, citing Currituck County Will Book 2, pp.279–280. The manuscript was not inspected. The will also transfers an enslaved boy; that clause does not add a biological family relationship.

The reported 14 August 1805 death is inconsistent with a will executed on 14 October 1805. Prefer the qualified lower boundary after 14 October 1805, with the will’s recording on 22 January 1806 separately stated. Recording is not an exact death date. Preserve the former August claim as superseded imported information; inspect the manuscript to verify the copied dates. Birth and death place are unchanged.

Inspect Currituck Will Book 2, pp.279–280 and the estate/deed papers for the seven land recipients; trace Isaac’s fork-field inheritance to distinguish the two Isaac accounts. Seek an explicit older parent clause for William rather than transferring his children’s new confidence to the Caleb ancestry.
